title: Dating Convention: End of the Strip Use Period for Take-Backs, Blood Glucose Testing Supply Program
content:
The period over which a Blood Glucose Testing Supply Program customer is taken to have used held test strips ends on one of three dates.

**Convention.** The days of use end on the delivery date on the proof of delivery of the newest meter shipped on the program when that meter was delivered later than the latest strip refill was, by that refill's own proof of delivery; they end on the testing supplies program's hold start date when no newer meter was delivered later than that refill and the program went on hold later than that refill was delivered; otherwise they end today.

- The *newest meter* is the program's meter shipment with the latest ship date; its delivery date is the one on its own proof of delivery.
- The comparison is always with the delivery date on the latest strip refill's own proof of delivery.
- The *hold start date* is the date the program's current hold started, as the program record shows it.

**Input — judgement — end date (hypothetical dates; latest strip refill delivered 5 May)**

| Newest meter delivered | Program hold | End of the days of use |
|---|---|---|
| 1 June | none | 1 June |
| 1 June | hold started 20 May | 1 June — a later meter delivery comes first |
| 3 May | hold started 20 May | 20 May |
| 5 May | none | today — a meter delivered the same day is not later |
| not delivered yet | hold started 1 May | today — the hold did not start later than the refill was delivered |
| not delivered yet | none | today |
